title: lsp-first-read-guard deadlocks workers with no LSP tool
description:
HARNESS, not game code. ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js blocks Read on code files until an LSP warmup call, but never checks whether the agent HAS the LSP tool. Subagents frequently do not: one implementer reported 'ToolSearch found no LSP tool at all, for any query' while the hook still blocked Read. The only remaining way to read a file is 'bash cat', which rules/tool-discipline.md forbids — there is no legal move.

Second defect: the state flag is ~/.claude/state/lsp-ready-<md5(cwd)>, keyed on cwd ONLY. agentId is not in the PreToolUse payload and all subagents share the session's sessionId, so concurrent workers in one repo share ONE read budget. Verified: agents a7257c13c1cd759f4 and ad87181ae55be8f94 (identical promptId d2aea593, same cwd, 27s apart) drew from one counter; one hit 'Gate 5 — Read #6 requires at least 2 LSP navigation calls' having made only one nav call itself.

Impact measured on session a4b9c11d: 4 of 15 workers hard-blocked, 7 mentioned the guard or missing LSP. NOBODY reported it as a blocker — they silently degraded to bash cat, so tool discipline was being violated wave-wide and invisibly.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by keying the flag per-agent. The payload does not carry an agent id; it cannot be done.

FIX (written and tested, NOT installed — global user config needs Caio's go-ahead):
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-caio-soviet-simulator/a4b9c11d-b7b9-453d-a0ca-3d7e14efbd86/scratchpad/lsp-first-read-guard.patched.js
Adds a per-file consecutive-block counter; after 2 blocks on the same file it relents with a loud systemMessage instead of blocking forever, and a successful read clears that file's counter. An agent that actually calls LSP never reaches the hatch.

VERIFIED STANDALONE (fake HOME, clean state):
  deadlock case, same Read retried 4x -> exit 2, exit 2, exit 0 (RELENTED), exit 0
  regression, warmup done -> .md exit 0 | read#1 exit 0 | read#2 exit 0 | read#3 exit 0 + WARNING | read#4 exit 2 Gate 4 | re-read exit 0
  node --check passes
Normal gate semantics are unchanged; only repeated blocks on one file relent.
close_reason: Patch installed 2026-08-24 at ~/.claude/hooks/lsp-first-read-guard.js (backup: .bak-2026-08-24). Per-file consecutive-block counter, RELENT_AFTER=2, applied at gates 1/4/5, counter cleared on any successful read. Differential smoke test in a real git repo outside the /tmp allow-list, HOME isolated: PATCHED -> block,block,RELENT,RELENT ; ORIGINAL -> block,block,block,block (deadlock confirmed). node --check OK. NOTE: the cwd-keyed shared read budget is NOT fixed - the PreToolUse payload carries no agent id, so concurrent subagents still share one counter. The relent path makes that survivable rather than fatal.

title: Verify the 370 SUBSTRATE claims in the requirements corpus
description:
GATE on every remaining iteration. The largest known liability in the project, and nothing tracked it until now.

Every AC in requirements/EPIC-*.md carries a [SUBSTRATE: ...] tag asserting what the code already provides. Measured 2026-08-23:

  370 ACs carry a tag        103 cite an exact file:line
  265 ABSENT   33 CONFLICTS   26 PROVIDED   19 PARTIAL   17 UNAUDITED   10 OURS

NOT ONE HAS EVER BEEN VERIFIED. The extraction wrote them from spec prose. iterative-development's PAR reviews asked "what is missing?", never "is this true?". The format even has a tag literally named UNAUDITED.

WHY THIS IS P1: every serious failure of 2026-08-23 was a wrong substrate claim.
  - "extend map_dynamic::Dispatcher" - truck registration was commented out; the dispatcher had never seen a truck. The agent built the mechanism the AC forbade.
  - "copy the freight_station train pattern" - trains have no parking layer; trucks only move when Driving with a Transporter collider. Premise false.
  - base_mod/items.lua sets optout_exttrade on 1 item of 21. That line falsified three claims in a landed commit.
Each cost 110-155k tokens. The next 122 stories are briefed off this same unverified corpus.

HOW: dispatch substrate-cartographer over the 103 file:line citations first - they are mechanically checkable. For each, record VERIFIED / STALE / WRONG with the current file:line. Then the 26 PROVIDED and 33 CONFLICTS tags, which carry the most weight because briefs act on them.

DO NOT rewrite the ACs wholesale. Record the verification result alongside; a wrong tag is a finding for the lead to disposition, not a licence to edit a ratified requirement.

TRAP: some tags cite W&R reference constants (e.g. $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE) copied from spec/citizens.md. The real corpus is on disk at ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/SovietRepublic/media_soviet/buildings_types/ - 1,472 .ini files, $CITIZEN_ABLE_SERVE appears 53 times. Those are checkable too.

title: Dispatches wedge: bakeries have no trucks but every bread purchase creates one
description:
Three unbounded-wait dispatch states, none with a timeout or cancellation. The dispatches Vec grows without bound and is walked every tick.

(c) IS THE GAMEPLAY-BREAKING ONE: every human bread purchase now creates a Dispatch, but bakeries are kind="store" (base_mod/companies.lua:11,126) and goods_company.rs:129 spawns trucks ONLY `if ckind == CompanyKind::Factory`. VERIFIED. So a city's bakeries accumulate one permanently-reserved dispatch per unfilled meal. Worse: recipe_should_produce reads RAW capital, not capital-reserved, so the bakery also stops producing while holding stock it can never sell.

(a) Loading with no route to buyer (market.rs:520-537): door_pos(buyer) returns None once the buyer's building is demolished; ticks_left is already 0 so it retries forever. The seller was ALREADY debited at ToSource arrival - quantity permanently destroyed. The truck is never dispatcher.free'd (only happens at market.rs:557), so it leaks too.

(b) ToSource with truck: Some(v) where the vehicle entity is gone: world.vehicles.get(v) -> None -> .unwrap_or(false) (market.rs:494-499) -> never arrives. reserved[seller] frozen forever.

FIX: needs a cancellation/timeout path. Consider also whether stores should get trucks, or whether human purchases should create dispatches at all.

Option C (no store->consumer dispatches, eat-time settlement), event-driven cancellation both Market::remove halves, MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES bound, dead-seller truck free. Proof: cargo test -p simulation 42 passed/0 failed (parallel + serial); both new tests mutation-proven red by implementer AND independently re-run red by opus gate; ledger CONSERVED (r3, r4 adds no surface); opus APPROVE; codex cross-review SEND-BACK adjudicated — both new findings pre-fork, filed sov-jcl/sov-xyx. title: Ext-trade surplus sale double-spends reserved stock
description:
LEDGER BROKEN. Units created from nothing during ordinary gameplay.

market.rs:398-410 (ext-trade surplus loop) reads `capital` and NEVER reads `reserved`. `reserved` is read in exactly ONE place in the crate: the domestic filter_map at market.rs:319-322.

SUBTLETY - the domestic loop is NOT the bug. It decrements sorder.qty as it reserves, so within ONE make_trades pass the ext block sees order.qty == capital - reserved and closes correctly. The hole is `sell_all` (market.rs:191): it re-posts the order at FULL capital and forgets the reservation. recipe_act calls it every production cycle (goods_company.rs:56-61), so the overwrite is routine.

BREAK WINDOW: final capital = stock - reserved, negative iff reserved > stock. Production requires capital < amount*(mult+1) and reserved <= capital, so the window is amount*mult < capital < amount*(mult+1). EMPTY for amount=1. OPEN for amount=10.

REAL PROTOTYPE THAT HITS IT: base_mod/companies.lua flour-factory, production {{"flour",10}}, storage_multiplier=5 -> stock 50, gate capital<60, window 50<capital<60. VERIFIED present.

Sequence: F capital 59, domestic matches 55 (reserved=55, sorder.qty=4, capital still 59). recipe_act produces +10 -> 69, sell_all overwrites order to qty 69/stock 50. Next pass ext-trade: qty_sell = 69-50 = 19, guard passes, capital -> 50, 19 exported for real money. Trucks arrive, Loading debits 55 -> capital = -5. 69 units existed; 55 delivered + 19 exported = 74. FIVE CREATED FROM NOTHING.

Then capital<0 makes sell_all bail (c<=0), so the loss is silently absorbed as lost production.

FIX: guard and compute surplus against `*cap - reserved` / `order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved)`, or make sell_all post capital-reserved.

ALSO IN THIS BLOCK (separate, pre-existing): market.rs:387-396 credits the buyer BEFORE checking find_external. mod.rs:69-78 returns None when world.freight_stations is empty. So with no freight station - normal early game - every unmatched buy order is granted free every tick, no money debited, no Trade recorded so it does not even appear in EcoStats. Scarcity is off. FIX: move the credit inside the Some(ext) arm.
close_reason: commit fdfabca: ext-trade surplus computed against order.qty.saturating_sub(reserved) and guarded on *cap - reserved; buy-order credit moved inside the Some(ext) arm. title: simulation test binary segfaults under parallel test threads
description:
GATE on evidence reliability. PRE-EXISTING - reproduced on an unmodified tree (1 in 5 runs), NOT introduced by ITER-0000.

SYMPTOM: 'cargo test -p simulation' with default parallel threads segfaults intermittently (SIGSEGV, no Rust backtrace - a raw crash, not a panic). Reproduces ~1-in-3 to 1-in-5.

ROOT CAUSE: crate::init::init() (simulation/src/init.rs:33) pushes into 'static mut' INIT_FUNCS / GSYSTEMS / SAVELOAD_FUNCS with no synchronization. Every TestCtx::new() called it unconditionally, so concurrent test threads race on those pushes. rustc already warns here: 'creating a mutable reference to mutable static ... undefined behavior'.

PARTIAL FIX ALREADY IN TREE: TestCtx::new() now guards the init::init() call with std::sync::Once (simulation/src/tests/mod.rs). This REDUCES but does NOT eliminate the crash - some other unsynchronized global path is also involved and was not chased, to respect the do-not-touch-adjacent-code rule.

WORKAROUND until fixed: run 'cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1'. All ITER-0000 verification used it.

WHY P1: the iterative-development spine treats sentinel scenario runs as evidence. A suite that segfaults 1-in-5 produces a confidently wrong signal - a green run proves little and a red run gets blamed on the wrong change. Fix before the sentinel corpus grows.

TRAP: do not 'fix' this by making the tests single-threaded in CI config and calling it done. That hides the UB rather than removing it; the static mut pattern is the defect.

comments.author: kornai-economist
comments.text:
KORNAI PHASE-0 RULING — sov-lpj: how request-inflation is declared and arises

VERDICT: HYBRID, but with a hard sequencing rule. Ship the STATIC Lua-declared
propensity for 1.0. Design the sim modulation so it is ADDITIVE later; do NOT
build it now. Reasons and rejections below.

== 1. THE AXIS RULING ==

REJECTED: pure emergent inflation (sim raises requests in response to
experienced shortage) as the 1.0 mechanism.

Kornai is on the lead's side theoretically -- hoarding IS a response to supply
uncertainty ("the firm... strives to build up reserves of input stocks",
Economics of Shortage, on the hoarding-shortage vicious circle). But three
things kill it as the 1.0 mechanism:

(a) OBSERVABILITY. A globally emergent rule makes every enterprise inflate by
roughly the same amount at roughly the same time. The Planner cannot detect a
liar when everyone lies identically -- the discrepancy stops being a signal and
becomes a constant offset on the whole economy. Detection needs VARIANCE across
enterprises, and variance needs a per-prototype declaration. This is the
"observable" test from the model: a deception the player cannot distinguish
from background is noise, not gameplay.

(b) It is a FEEDBACK LOOP, and the shortage signal it would read is currently
untrustworthy (see section 4). An emergent rule wired to a broken scarcity
signal produces either runaway inflation or none.

(c) SCOPE. The charter binds. An adaptive-expectations layer is a system, not a
field. Nothing in charter 1.0 §Resources-and-production commits to it.

REJECTED: a per-company random roll at spawn. It gives variance but it is not
authored, not reproducible across saves for the same city, and gives the
Planner nothing to learn -- the player can never build a model of WHICH
enterprises lie, only re-check all of them every time. That is chores, not
inference.

ACCEPTED: static per-prototype declaration, sim reads it at recipe_init and
recipe_act. Authored variance across the 26 companies. Reproducible.
Learnable ("the meat-facility always over-orders"). Cheapest thing that makes
the loop real.

== 2. DATA SCHEMA SKETCH ==

Lua, on the RECIPE table (base_mod/companies.lua), NOT on the company:

    recipe = {
        consumption = {{"cereal", 1}},
        production  = {{"flour", 10}},
        duration = "100s",
        storage_multiplier = 5,
        request_multiplier = 3,     -- NEW, optional, default 1
    }

Rust: `prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs` -- add to `struct Recipe`

    /// How much input this enterprise REQUESTS per cycle, as a multiple of what
    /// its recipe actually consumes. 1 = honest. >1 = inflates its requirement
    /// and hoards the surplus. There is no honesty flag: the Planner infers
    /// dishonesty from stock that outruns consumption.
    pub request_multiplier: i32,   // default 1 when absent

parsed with the existing get_lua pattern, defaulted (NOT `get_lua(...)?` --
absent must mean 1, or all 26 companies break).

Sim wiring, `souls/goods_company.rs:21-27` and `:56-60`: the two existing
`.requested(soul, item.id).unwrap_or(item.amount as u32)` sites become the
requested value derived from `item.amount * recipe.request_multiplier`, with
`Market::set_requested` called ONCE at `recipe_init` so `Market::requested()`
becomes the single readable source for the panel. Do not compute it in two
places; the panel must read the same number the buy order used.

WHY ON THE RECIPE, NOT THE COMPANY: `requested` is per-item and only means
anything against a consumption amount. Recipe is where `consumption` and
`storage_multiplier` already live, and `recipe_init`/`recipe_act` already take
`&Recipe` and nothing else. A field on GoodsCompanyPrototype would have to be
threaded separately into both functions for no gain.

WHY A MULTIPLIER, NOT AN ABSOLUTE: with an absolute, a recipe amount change
silently turns an honest company dishonest. A multiplier keeps honesty
expressible as exactly one value (1) that survives rebalancing.

Per-item override is NOT needed for 1.0. All 26 companies consume 1-3 items at
amount 1; a whole-recipe multiplier expresses everything the current data can
show. If a later recipe needs to hoard cereal but not flour, add
`{"cereal", 1, request = 3}` then. Do not build it now.

== 3. MAGNITUDES -- and the important dynamics finding ==

CRITICAL: with `buy_until` (market.rs:414-420), a static multiplier produces a
BOUNDED hoard, not a growing one. buy_until tops up to N and stops. Steady
state for a company with consumption c and multiplier k is a standing stock
that oscillates in [k*c - c, k*c]: it holds k*c, consumes c, re-orders c.
The surplus is `(k-1)*c`, CONSTANT, reached after one delivery cycle.

This is the single most important number in this ticket and the acceptance
criteria must be written against it. "Surplus accumulates without bound" is
NOT what this mechanism does and a test asserting growth will fail.

Is a bounded hoard true to Kornai? YES, and this is the honest answer: the
firm's target reserve level is a stock, not a flow. What grows without bound in
Kornai is the SHORTAGE the hoard causes elsewhere, not the hoard itself. The
hoard is a permanent withdrawal of `(k-1)*c` units per hoarding enterprise from
the pool available to everyone else. That withdrawal is the gameplay.

Recommended 1.0 values, against the real base_mod data:
- Default 1 for all 26 companies (honest is the norm; a shortage economy where
  EVERY enterprise lies has no signal).
- Exactly 2-4 hoarders, on prototypes deep in the bread chain, where the
  Planner can trace the consequence downstream to a queue:
    * flour-factory (companies.lua:36, consumption cereal 1, production flour
      10) -- `request_multiplier = 4`. Standing hoard 3 cereal.
    * meat-facility (companies.lua:577, consumption raw-meat 1) --
      `request_multiplier = 3`. Standing hoard 2 raw-meat.
  Keep the bakery HONEST (consumption flour 1): it is the only store with
  production and the only item humans actually buy (bread, buyfood.rs:73). The
  contrast the panel needs is bakery-honest vs flour-factory-inflated one step
  upstream.
- Do not exceed 4. At amount 1 and storage_multiplier 5 the production-side cap
  is `capital - reserved < amount*(sm+1)` = 6; a request multiplier above the
  storage cap makes the enterprise permanently idle-with-full-larder, which
  reads as a bug, not a lie.

== 4. WHAT MAKES THE HOARD BITE -- the blocking dependency ==

A hoard is only meaningful if the withdrawn units were SCARCE. Verified on this
tree today (market.rs:650-680):

- The free-goods leak IS FIXED: `find_external` returning None now `continue`s
  BEFORE `*capital.entry(buyer) += qty_buy` (market.rs:667-671). Unmatched
  enterprise buy orders are no longer granted free when there are no freight
  stations. Good -- shortage exists in the early game.
- BUT once a freight station exists, every unmatched non-human enterprise buy
  order is satisfied instantly from ext-trade: capital credited at market.rs:671
  with NO Dispatch (the dispatch loop at market.rs:604 has already run over
  `all_trades[dispatch_start..]`; ext trades are pushed after it). Goods
  teleport, and the enterprise never experiences shortage.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: the hoard is invisible in any city with a freight
station, because nobody downstream ever goes short -- ext-trade backfills them
for free at the border price. The Planner sees a fat larder with no victim. The
mechanic is technically present and dramatically inert.

I am NOT asking sov-lpj to fix that. I am asking that it be filed and that
sov-lpj's acceptance be written to demonstrate the hoard in a NO-freight-station
city, so the ticket cannot be closed against a build where scarcity is bypassed.
File the teleport as a separate bead (successor to sov-ledger-exttrade-cbh).

== 5. THE FIVE DISCREPANCIES -- what 1.0 needs ==

REQ-PRODUCTION-001 names request, receipt, consumption, surplus, age.
For 1.0, in sim state:

MUST EXIST (1.0):
- REQUEST -- `Market::requested()`. Exists. This ticket gives it a real value.
- CONSUMPTION -- derived, `recipe.consumption[i].amount`. Exists; no new state.
- SURPLUS -- derived, `capital - reserved - consumption`. No new field. The
  panel differences it. Do NOT add a stored surplus field; a stored one can
  drift from the truth and the whole point is that the number is inferred.

DEFER (post-1.0, or later ticket -- each is a new accumulator, i.e. new state
that must be serialized, migrated and kept consistent):
- RECEIPT (cumulative delivered) -- a new per-company per-item counter. Adds
  save-format surface. It is a nicer signal than surplus but it is not needed:
  with a static multiplier, surplus alone separates honest from dishonest
  unambiguously (honest surplus = 0 in steady state, dishonest = (k-1)*c > 0).
- AGE (how long stock has sat) -- requires per-unit or per-lot timestamps, i.e.
  turning capital from a scalar into a queue. That is a substantial change to
  the Market representation and is the single most expensive of the five. It is
  the RIGHT long-term signal (stagnant stock is the true tell) and it is where
  the emergent version eventually lives, but it is not 1.0.

Ruling: THREE of five for 1.0 (request, consumption, surplus), two deferred.
This still satisfies the binding sentence "let the Planner infer hoarding
without an honesty flag" -- inference from three quantities is inference.

== 6. MODEL CHECKS ==

1. Clears by queue, not price? YES. `request_multiplier` changes a QUANTITY on
   a buy order. No Money anywhere on this path; `Trade.money_delta` stays
   Money::ZERO for domestic matches (market.rs:528). A richer enterprise gets
   nothing faster. CONSISTENT.
2. Preserves shortage? STRENGTHENS it, and is in fact the first mechanism in
   the game that manufactures shortage endogenously rather than from
   under-building. This is Kornai's hoarding-shortage vicious circle made
   playable. CONSISTENT -- conditional on section 4.
3. Failure degrades? YES. A hoarded input means the downstream plant idles and
   the queue lengthens. No termination path is introduced. CONSISTENT.
4. Preserves the incentive to lie? This is the one weakness, stated plainly:
   a STATIC multiplier is not an incentive, it is a fact. The enterprise does
   not choose to lie; it was authored lying. Honesty is not costly-or-cheap, it
   is just a number. The core loop's EMOTIONAL truth -- "this is rational
   behaviour under the incentives, not villainy" -- is asserted by the fiction,
   not produced by the sim.
   I accept this for 1.0 anyway. The Planner-facing half of the loop (catch it
   from observable state) is fully real with a static field, and that is the
   half the player touches. The enterprise-facing half (choose to lie because
   honesty gets you shorted) is where the emergent version belongs, post-1.0,
   and section 2's schema is deliberately shaped so it can arrive as
   "request_multiplier becomes the FLOOR/propensity, sim raises it under
   experienced shortage" without a data migration.
   State this trade-off in the bead. Do not let it be discovered later as a
   surprise.
5. Observable? YES, and by INFERENCE not readout, provided the panel shows
   requested and true consumption as separate numbers and does NOT show a
   "dishonest: yes/no" badge or a pre-computed inflation factor. The player
   must do the subtraction. Hard constraint on the downstream UI story
   (sov-hoard-panel-mko).

== 7. ACCEPTANCE-SHAPING CONSTRAINTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION BEAD ==

A. `request_multiplier` is OPTIONAL in Lua and defaults to 1. A parse that
   requires it breaks all 26 existing companies. Test: an unmodified company
   prototype still loads.
B. At least two shipped prototypes in base_mod/companies.lua declare
   request_multiplier > 1 (recommend flour-factory 4, meat-facility 3), so a
   running game -- not a fixture -- contains hoarders. This is the AC that
   sov-lpj exists for.
C. `Market::set_requested` gains at least one PRODUCTION caller. Test that
   fails if it goes back to test-only: assert requested() != None for a
   company spawned through company_soul in a live sim.
D. The surplus assertion must be BOUNDED, not growing: after N>=2 delivery
   cycles, an enterprise with multiplier k and consumption c holds stock in
   [k*c - c, k*c], and an honest one holds <= c. Mutation proof: set the
   hoarder's multiplier to 1 and the test must fail.
E. Demonstrated in a city with NO freight station. If ext-trade can backfill,
   the hoard has no victim and the test proves nothing about shortage.
F. NO honesty flag, NO stored surplus field, NO derived "inflation percentage"
   in sim state. Request and consumption are stored/declared; surplus is
   differenced at read time.
G. NO Money on any touched path. Negative assertion, enforced not merely
   written: assert money_delta == Money::ZERO for the domestic matches in the
   scenario.
H. Do not touch `storage_multiplier` semantics. request_multiplier bounds the
   INPUT buy order; storage_multiplier bounds the OUTPUT cap
   (goods_company.rs:41). They are the W&R $STORAGE_IMPORT / $CONSUMPTION
   distinction and must stay separate.

Two W&R notes: W&R has no field expressing "requests more than it consumes" --
confirmed, this is our invention, nothing to copy. But W&R's separation of
$CONSUMPTION (rate) from $STORAGE_IMPORT (inbound buffer, per transport class,
e.g. asphalt plant: $CONSUMPTION gravel 25 / $STORAGE_IMPORT
RESOURCE_TRANSPORT_GRAVEL 30) is the exact precedent for keeping our declared
request separate from our declared consumption. We are adding a third
quantity -- the REPORTED requirement -- that W&R does not have, and that is
precisely the design's contribution.

-- kornai-economist, Phase 0 consult, verified against working tree 2026-08-26

title: The design pillars have no runtime assertions
description:
Both pillars were violated in shipped code and no test noticed.

"Nothing teleports" and "never game over" are stated in CLAUDE.md, encoded as prose in ACs, and enforced NOWHERE at runtime.

EVIDENCE: the ext-trade buy block credited a buyer their full requested quantity whenever find_external returned None - which it does whenever world.freight_stations is empty, the normal early game. Every unmatched buy order was granted free, every tick, unpaid, and absent from EcoStats. Scarcity, the entire pressure source of the design, was switched off. It compiled, passed review, and passed every test. Found only when a specialist agent traced conservation across the seam (commit fdfabca).

The conservation invariant in tests/scenarios/ledger.rs is the first assertion of a pillar in the codebase and it only covers quantity.

PROPOSAL: give each pillar a cheap standing assertion the sentinel corpus runs every iteration.
  - nothing teleports: no capital increases without either a completed dispatch unload or a declared production/import source. Generalises ledger.rs beyond a hand-built pair of souls.
  - never game over: no code path terminates a run or produces an unrecoverable state; unmet need must always degrade.
  - clearing by queue, never by price: no Money read gates a physical flow. Partly a grep, better as a runtime assertion.

Cheaper than it sounds and it catches the class of bug that survives code review because the code is correct - it is the DESIGN that is violated.

If you take it: the two sites differ in that advance_dispatches counts return_route_retries against MAX_RETURN_ROUTE_RETRIES and Market::remove does not (it gets one attempt); do not accidentally give the remove path retries it never had, and do not drop the bound from the advance path.
acceptance_criteria: try_return_to_seller extracted and called from both sites; cargo test -p simulation still 42/42 green; the ledger-invariant-checker gate re-run returns CONSERVED; the retry-bound asymmetry between the two call sites is preserved or its change is deliberate and documented.

title: Retail claim-overwrite release is unsound once a second human-purchasable item exists (debug_assert is a release no-op)
description:
market.rs:503-531. When a human's RetailClaim is overwritten, the displaced claim's reservation is released using the per-kind loop's LOCAL 'reserved' map, guarded only by debug_assert_eq!(old.kind, kind) -- which compiles to nothing in release builds.

Sound TODAY only because buyfood.rs:82 is the sole issuer of human buy orders and hardcodes bread, so old.kind always equals kind. The moment a second human-purchasable item exists, an overwrite across kinds silently decrements the WRONG market's reserved row in release builds: one seller's stock is unreserved without cause and another's stays frozen. Silent, no log, invisible to the ledger accountant (it is a reservation defect, not a capital one).

TRIGGER: any change that makes a human buy something other than bread. Fix at that time: look the correct SingleMarket up by old.kind instead of using the loop-local map, and turn the debug_assert into real branching.

Found by ledger-invariant-checker 3rd pass on sov-dispatch-wedge-ab4; explicitly flagged NOT a blocker for that ticket and left latent by lead decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) the release path looks the displaced claim's market up by old.kind rather than relying on the enclosing per-kind loop, with a test that overwrites a claim across two different item kinds and asserts both sellers' reserved rows are correct in a release-semantics build; or (b) a compile-time or runtime invariant makes a cross-kind overwrite impossible and is documented at the call site.

title: Give TestCtx a seed and a fast tick before the journey harness grows
description:
Two gaps found while reviewing the walking-skeleton harness plan.

1. NO SEED. SimulationOptions exposes only terrain_size and save_replay. JOURNEY-0001's final observable claims 'identical seed and inputs yield identical ledger figures', but there is no seed field - today that can only mean 'identical construction'. Either add a seed or reword the observable.

2. TICK COST. TestCtx::tick() does a full bincode encode + decode + per-key hashes() comparison EVERY tick. That is exactly the determinism guarantee we want, but it will dominate runtime on a multi-hundred-tick journey. Add a tick_fast() without the round-trip and keep the checked tick for boundaries.

Not blocking ITER-0000, which is short. Becomes painful as journeys lengthen.

Fast tick added: check_determinism() split out of tick(), advance_ticks(n) checks every 25th tick and always the last. Verified cargo test -p simulation -- --test-threads=1 -> 22 passed.
